title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
abstract: arXiv:2607.15209v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Multilingual pre-trained language models such as XLM-R perform well for major languages but struggle with low-resource Ge'ez-script languages, largely due to high out-of-vocabulary (OOV) rates and excessive subword fragmentation from Latin-script-centric tokenizers. We introduce VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R targeting Amharic and Tigrinya. We train language-specific SentencePiece tokenizers on curated monolingual corpora, extend XLM-R's vocabulary with 30k Ge'ez-script subwords, and initialize their embeddings via subword averaging. VEXMLM undergoes two-stage training: (1) continued masked language modeling on the curated corpora and (2) supervised fine-tuning on question answering, named entity recognition, and sentiment analysis. VEXMLM substantially outperforms XLM-R and Glot500 across all evaluated tasks on Amharic and Tigrinya, with particularly strong gains on out-of-vocabulary entity recognition. Critically, i

tldr: 该论文提出VEXMLM，通过扩展词汇和两阶段训练，显著提升了XLM-R在阿姆哈拉语和提格里尼亚语等低资源格厄兹文字语言上的性能，尤其在词汇外实体识别方面。
